potato early blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with ring patterns on the older leaves first, often with a yellow halo. Spots join up, leaves dry and drop, and tubers can get dark sunken patches.
look_alikes: Late blight (water-soaked, spreads very fast in cool wet weather)
Nutrient deficiency or natural ageing of lower leaves
potato early blight.favourable_weather: Warm weather with alternating wet and dry spells, dew or rain. Weak or nutrient-starved plants suffer more.

organic_control: Remove and destroy badly affected leaves and plants
Avoid overhead irrigation, and water at the base
Keep the crop well fed and not water-stressed
Hill up soil properly so tubers are covered
potato early blight.chemical_control: Use only a product that is registered in India for potato and this disease. Check the label or ask your agriculture officer for the product, dose and spray interval. No product or dose is given here.
prevention: Rotate with crops outside the potato, tomato, brinjal and chilli family
Clear old haulms and crop residue after harvest
Do not leave cull potatoes lying around
potato early blight.when_to_call_expert: If spots spread to many plants or the upper leaves, or if tubers show dark patches.

potato late blight.cause: Water mold (Phytophthora infestans), a fungus-like organism that also attacks tomato
potato late blight.symptoms: Water-soaked patches on leaves that turn brown to black, often with a pale green edge. In wet weather a white fuzzy growth shows on the underside of the leaf. Stems darken and the whole plant can collapse in a few days. Tubers get dry, brown, rotten patches and can rot in storage.
potato late blight.favourable_weather: Cool, cloudy, humid or foggy weather with rain or heavy dew, and leaves that stay wet for many hours. Hot, dry weather slows it down.

weather_profile.note: Moderate temperatures (about 15 to 27 C) with humidity near 90 percent or more and long leaf wetness, from university extension sources.

organic_control: Remove and destroy infected plants quickly, away from the field
Do not leave infected potatoes or plant parts in heaps near the field
Hill up soil well so tubers are not exposed to spores from the leaves
Dig and store only healthy-looking tubers, and sort out any with patches
potato late blight.chemical_control: Use only a product that is registered in India for potato and this disease. Protective sprays matter most in cool, wet spells, so ask your agriculture officer for the product, dose and spray interval. No product or dose is given here.
prevention: Remove volunteer potato plants and cull piles
Scout often in foggy or cool wet weather
Ask your KVK about varieties with some tolerance for your area
potato late blight.when_to_call_expert: At the first water-soaked patches, because the disease can destroy a crop within days in cool wet weather.
